question: Does GPP change more after a fertilisation than the weather of the same days explains?

openFindings: ANT-01, SAR-01, VII-01 (open): the raw stamps of Anttila, Sarkisuo and Viikki are UTC, but the build reads them as UTC+2. The local day of these sites is thus 2 hours early. The effect on 14-day window means is small (2 of 48 half hours per day move to the next day).
QVI-16 (open): Qvidja swc in frozen soil is not reliable. This script sets the daily swc to null when the daily soil temperature is 0 degC or less (all sites).

QVI-11 and QVI-07 (open): Qvidja NEE is probably a different processing version, and the provider GPP and Reco do not close with NEE. This dive uses the calculated GPP of data/calculated/daily.parquet.

figures.title: Change of daily GPP against the change of air temperature from the 14 days before to the 14 days after, for control pairs without management (grey) and for fertilisation episodes (colour), per site.
figures.desc: Three scatter panels with the same axes. X axis: change of the mean air temperature, after minus before (°C). Y axis: change of the mean daily GPP, after minus before (g C m-2 d-1). Haltiala: 239 control pairs from 5 years, slope of the temperature-only fit 0.95 g C m-2 d-1 per °C (r = 0.63), 5 fertilisation episodes. Qvidja: 246 control pairs from 7 years, slope of the temperature-only fit 0.20 g C m-2 d-1 per °C (r = 0.43), 4 fertilisation episodes. Viikki: 68 control pairs from 4 years, slope of the temperature-only fit 0.20 g C m-2 d-1 per °C (r = 0.40), 5 fertilisation episodes. Over all 14 fertilisation episodes, the observed GPP change has a mean of −0.07 (SD 4.14) and the change that the weather fit (temperature and light) gives has a mean of 2.24 g C m-2 d-1. In all panels, the GPP change of the control pairs increases with the temperature change. 10 of the 14 fertilisation episodes are below the temperature-only fit line of their site.

figures.title: Residual GPP change (observed minus the change that the weather fit of the control pairs gives) of each fertilisation episode, per site, with the 10 to 90 % range of the control residuals of the site.
figures.desc: Dot plot. X axis: residual of the daily GPP change, observed minus expected (g C m-2 d-1). Y axis: episodes grouped by site, labelled with the start date. Haltiala 5 episodes, control residuals 10 to 90 % from −4.73 to 6.43; Qvidja 4 episodes, control residuals 10 to 90 % from −1.63 to 1.97; Viikki 5 episodes, control residuals 10 to 90 % from −1.10 to 3.54. Mean residual of all 14 episodes −2.30 (SD 4.37, 95 % CI −4.63 to −0.18); fertilisation only −0.14 (n = 5); with tillage or sowing −3.51 (n = 9). 2 episodes rank above 90 % and 6 below 10 % of the control residuals of their site. 6 of the 14 residuals are inside the 10 to 90 % range of the control residuals of their site; 7 of the 9 episodes with tillage or sowing have a residual of zero or less.

figures.title: Mean course of daily GPP from 14 days before to 14 days after the start of the fertilisation episodes, in percent of the mean of the 14 days before, for episodes with fertilisation only and with tillage or sowing.
figures.desc: Two lines with a band of plus or minus one SD. X axis: day relative to the first day of the episode (-14 to +14, local days). Y axis: daily GPP in percent of the mean of days -14 to -1. Fertilisation only: 4 episodes; mean of days +10 to +14 228 % (mean of the daily SDs 214 %). With tillage or sowing: 7 episodes; mean of days +10 to +14 138 % (mean of the daily SDs 239 %). Days with fewer than 2 episodes are not shown. Episodes with a mean GPP before of less than 0.5 g C m-2 d-1 are not used. The spread between the episodes is large.
